newsitem.title: USA: Chevron opposes new clean air standards.
newsitem.headline: Chevron opposes new clean air standards.

text.p: Chevron Corp's chairman Wednesday urged shareholders to oppose proposed new clean air standards, saying the costs of the rules would far exceed any health benefits that might result.

"These proposed new standards...would cost business and U.S. consumers tens of billions of dollars -- far exceeding potential benefits," Kenneth Derr, chairman and chief executive officer of Chevron, told the company's annual meeting.
Derr was referring to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) considering tougher pollution standards than those now in place under the Clean Air Act of 1990.
The agency will likely impose the standards later this year after a period of public review.

"If you feel, as I do, that these standards are not needed to protect health, and are, in fact, harmful to the U.S. economy, I urge you to write to both your state and federal elected officials," Derr said.
